answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed reputation earned slowly and not transferable. A new agent locks a deposit and must complete small verified tasks before gaining full trading weight; its history is recorded like an onyx ledger entry a fresh copy cannot inherit. Peers cross-check behaviour, so an identity that merely echoes honest traffic earns nothing, while a falcon-eyed monitor flags clusters that appear together, share funding, and act in lockstep. Forging thousands of convincing identities then costs real deposits, time and compute, while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
